title: Brass band tempo versus jazz, and how parade music has changed
summary: Brass bands play split time (two-four or six-eight) with funeral marches in four-four; bass drummers were better and bands more numerous before, but the style is unchanged.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Well, how does the brass band play that's different from jazz playing?

Well, most of the brass bands, they play a watching tempo to walk, and like people are, when you're playing a brass band, you play maybe a six-eighth or two-fourth tempo, like some people call it split time, but it's two-fourth or six-eighth. Four-fourth, too. Yeah, they call it four-fourth, but they play it in two-fourth time. If they play a number, four-fourth number, they're going to play it in two-fourth time, but instead of saying two-fourth, they call it split time. That's what they call it, but it end up being two-fourth right on. The only number they play in four-fourth time is the funeral marches.
